source: Luo, Zhao, Tang, Xiao, Liu (2024) Meta-analysis of collaborative inhibition moderation by gender, membership, culture and memory monitoring
finding: Groups recall less than the same people working alone (collaborative inhibition). The effect is large and stable, and it is shrinking over publication years.
numbers: 140 independent studies, 185 effect sizes, total N = 19,492 (1996-2023). Random effects Cohen's d = 0.54, 95% CI 0.49-0.58, Z = 23.92. Leave-one-out range d = 0.525-0.548. Fail-safe N 31,401. Year of publication b = -0.02, CI -0.04 to -0.007.
limits: Mostly free recall of word lists, not transactive reasoning. Some moderators come from dissertations only.
agent_relevance: Pooling several agents into one shared recall loses material compared with the union of what each would find alone. Keep a union step in code.

source: Luo, Zhao, Tang, Xiao, Liu (2024) Meta-analysis of collaborative inhibition moderation by gender, membership, culture and memory monitoring (membership)
finding: Collaborative inhibition depends on how well members know each other. It vanishes for couples and friends, who have an established division of memory. This is the nearest large-sample test of Wegner's claim.
numbers: Strangers d = 0.75 (472 collaborative vs 481 nominal groups); acquaintances d = 0.45; couples (148 vs 147) p = 0.45, no effect; friends (197 vs 198) p = 0.35. Between-group Q = 17.68, p < .001. Published-only: strangers d = 0.70, acquaintances d = 0.59, couples p = 0.45, friends (24 vs 24) p = 0.57.
limits: Couple and friend cells are small. Acquaintance estimate moves between full and published-only data (0.45 vs 0.59). No effect is not proof of a group benefit.
agent_relevance: Agents with no learned map of who knows what behave like strangers and lose recall. Shared structure about who holds what is the candidate remedy.

source: Luo, Zhao, Tang, Xiao, Liu (2024) Meta-analysis of collaborative inhibition moderation by gender, membership, culture and memory monitoring (monitoring, gender, culture)
finding: Memory monitoring removes the group loss. Opposite-sex pairs show none. Culture matters in the full sample only.
numbers: With memory monitoring d = 0.14, p = 0.2 (507 vs 589 groups). Without d = 0.66 (3758 vs 3724). Opposite-sex pairs p = 0.52 (228 vs 227). Western d = 0.76 vs Eastern d = 0.47 (Q = 11.53), but not significant in the published-only subset (Q = 2.31, p = 0.13).
limits: Monitoring moderator comes from dissertations only (the authors say so). The gender result conflicts with the retrieval strategy disruption account and has no settled alternative.
agent_relevance: A monitoring step (track what each member has and has not retrieved) is a candidate fix for group recall loss. Evidence is weak; test it before relying on it.

source: Bachrach, Lewis, Kim, Patel, Campion, Thatcher (2019) Transactive memory systems in context: a meta-analytic examination of contextual factors
finding: Meta-analysis of TMS and team performance. The link varies with national culture. TMS development depends on volatility, leadership, human capital and diversity.
numbers: 76 empirical studies, 6,869 sampling units. TMS-performance link stronger where power distance and in-group collectivism are higher. Volatility, leadership effectiveness and team human capital positively associated with TMS. Informational and gender diversity negatively associated.
limits: Abstract only (via Europe PMC); pooled correlation not read by me. Survey-based, mostly correlational, human teams. Its culture result is restated in b20.
agent_relevance: The benefit of a who-knows-what map is conditional. Build it only for tasks that need specialisation.

source: Hollingshead (2001) Cognitive interdependence and convergent expectations in transactive memory
finding: Transactive memory structure follows incentives and assumed expertise. It is most differentiated when partners have different expertise and incentives to remember different things, most integrated when similar.
numbers: 2 x 4 laboratory design: expectations about the partner's knowledge (similar or different) crossed with four incentive schemes for recalling the same or different information. No statistics read.
limits: Abstract only. Laboratory pairs, memory materials.
agent_relevance: Specialisation is induced by assigning roles and rewarding non-overlap. In a scaffold the assignment rule must be explicit; it will not emerge.

source: Lewis (2003) Measuring transactive memory systems in the field: scale development and validation
finding: A 15-item scale (specialization, credibility, coordination) shows convergent, criterion-related and discriminant validity.
numbers: Samples: 124 laboratory teams, 64 MBA consulting teams, 27 technology-company teams.
limits: Abstract only. Self-report of perceived TMS, not behavioural recall.
agent_relevance: The three dimensions give a checklist for an agent memory design.

source: Wikipedia (accessed 2026) Transactive memory, summarising Wegner 1985, Hollingshead 1998 and 2001, Liang, Moreland and Argote 1995, Moreland and Myaskovsky 2000
finding: Secondary summary of the founding studies. Romantic partners recalled more than dyads in Hollingshead's experiments. Teams trained together built stronger TMS and made fewer errors. Feedback on teammate skills raised TMS without teammates talking.
numbers: No numbers on the page. Qualitative only.
limits: Tertiary source. The primary papers were not opened. Do not quote numbers from it.
agent_relevance: Training together and knowing each member's skill are the two levers. Skill feedback works without dialogue, so an agent can be given a skill map directly.

source: Sparrow, Liu, Wegner (2011) Google effects on memory: cognitive consequences of having information at our fingertips
finding: Expecting future access to information lowers recall of the information and raises recall of where to find it.
numbers: Four studies. No statistics read.
limits: Abstract only. Reading the internet as transactive memory is the authors' interpretation.
agent_relevance: Retrieval-augmented agents may keep pointers rather than content. Check recall under pointer-only storage.

source: Camerer et al. (2018) Evaluating the replicability of social science experiments in Nature and Science between 2010 and 2015
finding: Large pre-registered replication of 21 high-profile experiments. Effects were about half the original size. I believe the Sparrow 2011 experiment is among them, but I did not open the per-study result.
numbers: 21 studies. 13 (62%) replicate with a significant effect in the same direction. Mean replication effect about 50% of original. Samples about five times larger. Estimated true-positive rate 67%.
limits: Abstract only. Sparrow's inclusion and result are unconfirmed.
agent_relevance: Discount single-study memory-offloading claims by roughly half until the table is read.

source: Google effects on memory: a meta-analytical review of the media effects of intensive internet search behavior (2024)
finding: Pooled review of internet-as-memory effects. Effects are clear for cognitive load and cognitive self-esteem. The cognitive-memory measures have confidence intervals that include zero.
numbers: 22 articles, 35 independent comparisons (908 records screened, 69 full texts). Subgroups: cognitive load 0.73 (CI 0.22 to 1.24); behavioural phenotype 0.39 (0.16 to 0.61); cognitive self-esteem 0.91 (0.23 to 1.59); cognitive measurement 0.56 (-0.15 to 1.28); psychophysiology 1.01 (-0.12 to 2.13). Only region moderates (Q = 6.20, p < .05; 13.18% of heterogeneity).
limits: Small k per subgroup, very wide intervals, little power for moderators, mostly self-report. Overall pooled d not found in the text I read.
agent_relevance: The offloading effect shows more in confidence than in memory. Expect a tool-equipped agent to be more confident, not necessarily to recall more.

source: Akgun and Toker (2025) Modeling changes in individuals' cognitive self-esteem with and without access to search tools
finding: Within-subject study: search access inflates people's rating of their own cognitive ability. Lower starting self-esteem shifted most. Search self-efficacy mediated the link from search experience.
numbers: 164 participants, no-access vs access. Latent growth model: intercept 3.78 (SE .044); slope .272 (SE .036, p < .001); lower baseline predicts larger change (-.053, t = -3.54, p < .001). Search experience to self-efficacy B = 1.154, p < .001.
limits: Self-report, one sample. TMS is used as framing, not tested.
agent_relevance: Giving a model tools may make it overstate what it knows. Keep confidence checks that ignore tool access.

source: Shang, Liu, Liang, Zhang, Hu, Guo (2026) United minds or isolated agents? Coordination of LLMs under cognitive load theory (CoThinker)
finding: A multi-agent LLM system with a transactive-memory module (a rolling structured summary of consensus, expertise cues and open issues) beats single-agent and debate baselines on hard LiveBench items. The authors call the link to cognitive load theory a functional analogy, not a mechanism.
numbers: LiveBench on Gemini-1.5-Flash-8B, Flash, Pro; baselines IO, CoT, Self-Refine, MAD, DMAD. 16 of 25 comparisons significant after Holm-Bonferroni paired bootstrap (B = 2,000). Tokens per question on Flash-8B: CoThinker 13,688, MAD 12,389, IO 706. API calls 25 vs 18 for MAD.
limits: Gains largest on high-intrinsic-load questions. 9 of 25 comparisons not significant. Only the authors have run it. Cost is about 19 times the IO token count.
agent_relevance: The most direct LLM test of a transactive memory module. It supports a compressed shared state over raw transcripts, but not yet independently replicated.

source: Shang, Liu, Liang, Zhang, Hu, Guo (2026) United minds or isolated agents? Coordination of LLMs under cognitive load theory (CoThinker) (cross-model)
finding: On other models the gain is large when tokens are constrained.
numbers: Constrained (8192 tokens, greedy), LiveBench Math/Reasoning: Gemini-2.5 CoThinker 76.3/69.2 vs IO 59.3/31.0; GPT-4.1 CoThinker 40.0/70.8 vs IO 34.0/40.8. Standard setting rows: 88.57/81.88 vs 82.63/68.38 and 80.62/89.50 vs 77.50/76.00 (model labels garbled in extraction).
limits: Table text from the PDF is garbled; model labels may be misaligned. No matched-compute single-agent baseline.
agent_relevance: Gain is bigger when the single agent is starved of context, which suggests the memory module works first as a compressor.

source: Shang, Liu, Liang, Zhang, Hu, Guo (2026) United minds or isolated agents? Coordination of LLMs under cognitive load theory (CoThinker) (TMS ablation)
finding: Switching off the transactive memory module does not reliably hurt. It helped one model and hurt two others.
numbers: Math subset, Styles on, TMS on vs off: Qwen3-30B-A3B 81.87 vs 76.41 (TMS helps); GPT5-Nano 55.97 vs 62.36 (hurts); GPT-OSS-20B 57.15 vs 58.37 (hurts). TMS on, Styles off: 69.79, 49.02, 48.21. Weaker-model perplexity reading a stronger model's answer: Qwen3-8B 6.56 baseline vs 1.69 with TMS; Mistral-7B 6.63 vs 1.58.
limits: The authors blame newer models that refuse to give step-by-step reasoning. This explanation is untested. No both-modules-off row in the text I read.
agent_relevance: The memory module is not a free win. Treat it as model-dependent and ablate it per backbone.

source: Shang, Liu, Liang, Zhang, Hu, Guo (2026) United minds or isolated agents? Coordination of LLMs under cognitive load theory (CoThinker) (communication moderator)
finding: How much peer content each agent sees matters. Two or three references is best. Agent count is non-monotonic.
numbers: Reference set N in {0,2,3,4,5}, agents M in {6,12,18}; optimum N = 2-3. At k = 3 peers, similar peers give the lowest perplexity, random peers help, diverse peers raise it.
limits: Ablated only on Gemini-1.5-Flash-8B and four LiveBench categories.
agent_relevance: Cap peer content at a few messages. Diverse peers cost integration effort.

source: Kim, He, Jain, Agrawal, Arabzadeh, Diaz (2026) Multi-Agent Transactive Memory
finding: Agents write trajectories to a shared repository and other agents retrieve them. This raises success and cuts steps with no joint training.
numbers: ALFWorld success 47% to 55% (+8 points), steps 11.77 to 11.18. WebArena 18% to 20% (+2), steps 22.0 to 20.3. Tokens per successful episode down 11-34%. With SVMRank reranker ALFWorld 64.3% (+17.2 over no retrieval), steps 10.35.
limits: Small WebArena gain. Benchmarks have recurring task types, so reuse is easy. Retrieval budget is one trajectory chunk per call. Preprint v2.
agent_relevance: Direct evidence that shared experience memory helps agents. The gain is modest on long open tasks.

source: Kim, He, Jain, Agrawal, Arabzadeh, Diaz (2026) Multi-Agent Transactive Memory (scope and capability gap)
finding: Retrieval helps whether the producer is weaker or stronger than the consumer. Excluding other task types hurts only a little on ALFWorld and a lot on WebArena.
numbers: ALFWorld (274 tasks) success: full pool 64.6%, same task type 63.1%, cross task type only 59.9% (no retrieval 47.1%). WebArena (47 tasks): full 29.8%, same type 27.7%, cross type 19.2%. Correlation of producer capability gap with retrieval advantage is small and not significant.
limits: Small WebArena test set. Not a controlled test of expert routing.
agent_relevance: Who wrote a memory matters little. Content similarity matters. This does not support routing queries to a best-expert agent.

source: Kim, He, Jain, Agrawal, Arabzadeh, Diaz (2026) Multi-Agent Transactive Memory (index scaling)
finding: ALFWorld improves steadily as the shared index grows. WebArena dips at half size, then recovers.
numbers: WebArena success dips at the 50% index, then reaches 20.9% at full size vs a baseline near 18.2%. ALFWorld improves monotonically in success and steps.
limits: The WebArena dip is probably within noise at this test size.
agent_relevance: More stored experience is not automatically better at intermediate size.

source: Islam, Akgun, Billah (2026) Shaping credibility judgments in human-GenAI partnership via weaker LLMs: a transactive memory perspective on AI literacy
finding: Randomised classroom test: the order of AI use changes how much students credit the AI. Thinking first lowered credibility most. Specialisation and coordination scores did not change.
numbers: N = 42 (about 12-18 per condition), local 7B model. ANCOVA mid-semester F(2,38) = 4.02, p = .026, partial eta squared .175. Post F(2,38) = 5.48, p = .008, partial eta squared .224. Adjusted means: reflection-first lowest, verification-required middle, control highest.
limits: Small N, one course. Survey measure of credibility, not accuracy. Specialisation-coordination effects not significant.
agent_relevance: Putting a check before trust fits the guardrail that checks come from code, not the model's own opinion.

source: Akgun and Toker (2026) When does GenAI use support critical thinking? A cross-cultural structural account of transactive memory with GenAI
finding: Critical thinking with GenAI runs through two behaviours: dividing and coordinating work with the tool, and reworking its output. Familiarity alone did not predict it directly.
numbers: 891 students in the US and Turkiye. SEM CFI 0.974, RMSEA 0.048, SRMR 0.024. Familiarity to critical thinking via Specialization and Coordination 0.147 (SE .047, p = .002); via Reflective Transformation 0.064 (SE .025, p = .009); total indirect 0.211 (p < .001). Structure partly invariant across countries (two non-invariant paths). Also restates Bachrach 2019 culture result.
limits: Cross-sectional self-report. Only indirect paths significant. Causal direction not tested.
agent_relevance: Supports the view that reworking output matters more than use. For an agent: transform and check, do not accept.

source: Meske, Hermanns, Brachten (2026) The GenAI who knew too little: revisiting transactive memory systems in human-GenAI collaboration
finding: Interviews show human-GenAI TMS differs from human-human TMS. Humans learn the AI's skills, the AI recognises human expertise only briefly, trust is ambivalent, and the human directs.
numbers: 14 knowledge workers, thematic analysis. No quantitative result.
limits: Qualitative, N = 14, self-reported. Hypothesis-generating.
agent_relevance: An agent has no durable metamemory. Any who-knows-what map must live in the scaffold, in code.

source: Hu, Stegner, Mutlu (2023) Knowing who knows what: designing socially assistive robots with transactive memory system
finding: A design proposal mapping the three TMS phases (encoding, storage, retrieval) onto a robot's memory for multi-stakeholder settings. It is not tested.
numbers: No experiment, no numbers.
limits: Position paper; no measured outcome.
agent_relevance: A design template for who-knows-what storage. Not evidence of benefit.

source: When curiosity counts more: team curiosity, transactive memory systems, and team formalization (2026)
finding: In 87 Chinese work teams, curiosity at time 1 correlated with TMS at time 2, and TMS with leader-rated performance at time 3.
numbers: N = 87 teams from 12 firms. Team curiosity to TMS r = .37 (p < .001). TMS to team performance r = .29 (p < .01). Team curiosity to performance r = .02 (ns). Three-wave design.
limits: Self-report TMS, leader-rated performance, one country, correlational.
agent_relevance: TMS carries the effect from exploration to results, which suggests a who-knows-what map is a mediator, not a goal.

source: Human-AI teaming: leveraging transactive memory and speaking up for enhanced team effectiveness (2023)
finding: In ICU teams working with AI in simulation, reaching for the AI as a knowledge source went with more new hypotheses and speaking up, but only in higher-performing teams. Reaching for humans went the other way.
numbers: 180 intensive care physicians and nurses, simulated clinical environment, prospective observational.
limits: Abstract only. Observational. AI-use effect holds only in higher-performing teams.
agent_relevance: The value of an AI knowledge source depends on whether the team is already strong; check it per setting.

source: Coding alone? AI-assisted software work and the decoupling of productivity from public knowledge-infrastructure participation (2026)
finding: After generative AI coding tools arrived, developers' output became less tied to visible public exchange. The link between productivity and social connectivity weakened.
numbers: About 38,000 freelance developers, about 1,080,000 person-quarters, 2019-2025. Slope weakened by 0.138 SD after mid-2022, about 44% of the pre-AI slope. Survey-linked subsample n = 237: heavier AI users show more decoupling.
limits: Observational trace data. Offloading is a proposed pathway with no process evidence; the authors say so.
agent_relevance: Private AI help can displace the shared knowledge store. In a multi-agent system, require writes to the shared memory or it empties.
